name: Wysa
summary: AI mental health chatbot that uses CBT and evidence-based tools to support anxiety, depression, and stress, with 4.6★ rating and published clinical evidence.
description: Wysa is an AI mental health app that uses a conversational chatbot, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) tools, and guided self-help exercises to help people manage anxiety, low mood, stress, and burnout. Users can talk to an AI penguin coach anytime, work through structured toolkits for specific problems, and optionally add human coaching or therapy. Multiple peer-reviewed studies have evaluated Wysa in real-world populations, and it has been used by millions of people worldwide.
patient_summary: Wysa is an AI ‘chatbot therapist’ you can talk to on your phone. It uses CBT-style questions, journaling prompts, and exercises to help with anxiety, low mood, stress, and burnout. You can work through packs for sleep, work stress, or relationships, and check in with your mood daily. There is a free version with core tools, plus paid options to chat with human coaches. It is not a replacement for a real therapist or crisis care, but can be a helpful self-care tool between sessions or while you’re on a waitlist.

linked_conditions.context: CBT-style thought-challenging, worry journaling, and grounding exercises can help people with mild to moderate generalized anxiety as an add-on to therapy or self-help.
CBT-based mood tracking and behavioral activation tools may help with mild depressive symptoms or relapse prevention, but are not a replacement for full treatment in moderate to severe depression.
Brief, situational distress due to life changes (work, relationship, medical diagnosis) can be supported with coping skills and problem-solving exercises in Wysa.

contraindications: Not a substitute for professional mental health treatment or crisis services.
Not appropriate as the sole intervention for moderate to severe depression, bipolar disorder, psychosis, or active suicidal thoughts.
People with trauma-related disorders may find some prompts triggering and should use Wysa alongside trauma-informed care.
Always contact emergency services or a crisis line in case of immediate risk of self-harm or harm to others.

sections.heading: What Wysa Does
sections.text: Wysa is an AI mental health chatbot you can message anytime. It uses CBT-style conversation, mood check-ins, and guided exercises to help you manage worry, low mood, stress, and burnout. You can work through structured ‘packs’ (for sleep, work stress, relationships, self-esteem), do daily reflections, and practice techniques like cognitive restructuring, breathing, and grounding. A paid upgrade offers human coaching or therapy in some regions.

sections.heading: How Well Does Wysa Work?
sections.comparison: Compared to baseline symptoms and expected course without structured support
sections.text: Peer-reviewed studies and real-world usage data suggest that people who actively use Wysa’s CBT tools and chatbot experience meaningful improvements in depression, anxiety, and stress scores on standard questionnaires such as PHQ-9 and GAD-7. Engagement studies show that many users continue returning to the app over weeks, suggesting that the format is acceptable and usable for day-to-day support.
sections.patient_text: Early research suggests that Wysa can be a helpful companion for managing everyday anxiety, low mood, and stress—especially when you use it regularly and combine it with other care (therapy, medication, or self-help). It is best thought of as a support tool, not a stand-alone cure.

sections.heading: Who Wysa Is Best For
sections.text: Wysa is best for people who:
items: Want a private, always-on place to talk through worries without judgment.
Have mild to moderate anxiety, low mood, or stress and want structured CBT-style tools.
Are on a therapy waitlist or between sessions and want extra support.
Prefer texting and chat-based support over long audio meditations.
Struggle with work stress, burnout, or perfectionism and want practical coping skills.
Like using mood trackers and journaling to reflect on patterns.
not_recommended: Anyone with active suicidal thoughts or a crisis—these situations need immediate human help, not a chatbot.
People with moderate to severe depression, psychosis, or bipolar disorder who need intensive clinical care.
People who strongly prefer face-to-face or video therapy and dislike chat-based interactions.
Users looking for a fully free human-therapy service (human coaching/therapy is a paid add-on).

items.description: You message a friendly penguin character that guides you through CBT-style questions, reframing thoughts, and problem-solving. The chatbot is available 24/7 and never gets tired.
items.evidence: Chat-based CBT and journaling are supported by decades of evidence for cognitive behavioral techniques and self-help approaches.

items.description: Curated collections of exercises for anxiety, low mood, work stress, relationships, and sleep. Packs combine psychoeducation, CBT techniques, and short practices.
items.evidence: Structured digital CBT programs have repeatedly shown benefit for mild to moderate anxiety and depression when used regularly.

items.description: Daily mood tracking and prompts help you notice patterns in thoughts, feelings, and behaviors over time.
items.evidence: Self-monitoring and mood tracking are standard CBT tools that support behavior change and relapse prevention.

items.description: Short exercises for grounding, breathing, relaxation, and mindfulness to use in the moment when you feel overwhelmed.
items.evidence: Brief skills-based interventions can reduce acute anxiety and help people tolerate distress in real-world situations.

items.description: In some regions, you can upgrade to text-based or live support from coaches or licensed clinicians who use Wysa’s tools as part of care.
items.evidence: Blended models (digital tools plus human support) often lead to better engagement and outcomes than self-help alone.

sections.heading: Privacy & Data Security
sections.summary: Wysa emphasizes privacy and secure handling of sensitive mental health conversations, and has been recognized by independent reviewers as one of the more privacy-respecting mental health apps.
items: End-to-end encryption for data in transit and secure storage of user data.
No selling of personal data to advertisers or data brokers.
Limited sharing of de-identified, aggregated data for service improvement and research.
Separate enterprise offerings for employers/health systems that include additional controls and agreements.
Clear, public privacy policy explaining what is collected and why.
data_collected: Account and contact information (such as email) to create and maintain your account.
Usage data about which tools you use and how often, to improve the app.
Chat content, processed by algorithms to provide responses and improve support.
Device and technical data (such as app version, OS, and crash logs).
data_shared: Payment information with payment processors for subscriptions.
Aggregated, de-identified analytics with partners for research and product improvement.
concerns: As with any digital mental health app, chat content can be sensitive, so users should review the privacy policy carefully.
Not a HIPAA-covered product for individual consumers; clinical deployments may have separate agreements.
sections.hipaa_note: Consumer use of Wysa is not generally covered under HIPAA. For clinical or enterprise deployments, organizations may have separate agreements and requirements.

sections.heading: How to Start Using Wysa
steps: Download Wysa from the App Store (iOS) or Google Play (Android).
Create an account using your email or preferred login method.
Complete the initial onboarding conversation so the chatbot can understand what you want help with.
Start with a simple goal—such as managing stress, improving sleep, or coping with low mood.
Do a short check-in with Wysa most days (even 5 minutes) to build the habit.
Explore toolkits (packs) for areas that matter most to you, like anxiety, work stress, or self-esteem.
If available in your region and appropriate for you, consider upgrading to human coaching or therapy for more support.
tips: Use Wysa regularly (a few times a week) rather than only in a crisis.
Be as honest as you feel comfortable—the AI doesn’t judge, and there’s no ‘perfect’ way to answer.
Combine Wysa with therapy or medical care if you already see a professional; bring insights from the app into your sessions.
Set gentle reminders on your phone to check in when stress is usually highest (for example, evenings after work).
common_mistakes: Expecting Wysa to act exactly like a human therapist—AI support feels different and is best used as a complement.
Using Wysa only once or twice and deciding it doesn’t work; most benefits come from repeated use over time.
Relying solely on the app when experiencing severe symptoms or crisis—in these situations, you need human help.
Skipping the structured packs and only chatting; the toolkits are where many of the specific CBT exercises live.

items.comparison: Another CBT-based AI chatbot focused on depression and anxiety. Woebot uses short, structured daily conversations; Wysa offers a broader toolkit-style experience and optional human coaching.
Better if you prefer guided audio meditations and structured mindfulness courses. Wysa is more chat-based and skills-focused rather than meditation-focused.
Great if you want simple mood tracking and visual patterns over time. Daylio is a tracker with journaling; Wysa adds an AI coach and CBT tools on top of mood logging.

faqs.q: Is Wysa a replacement for therapy?
faqs.a: No. Wysa is a self-care tool that uses an AI chatbot and CBT techniques to support your mental health. It can be a helpful supplement to therapy or medication, and useful while you’re waiting for care, but it is not a replacement for professional treatment—especially if you have moderate to severe symptoms or are in crisis.

faqs.q: What conditions can Wysa help with?
faqs.a: Wysa can help with everyday stress, worry, low mood, burnout, and mild to moderate symptoms of anxiety or depression. It is best for people who want support with coping skills and mindset shifts. If you have severe depression, bipolar disorder, psychosis, or thoughts of self-harm, you should seek in-person or live professional care instead of relying only on an app.

Wysa offers a free tier that includes core AI chatbot conversations, mood tracking, and some CBT tools. A paid subscription unlocks more toolkits and features, and in some regions you can add human coaching or therapy for an additional cost. Pricing varies by region and program—check inside the app for current details.

For most people with mild to moderate symptoms, using Wysa is safe and can feel more private than talking to others. However, it is important to remember that Wysa is an AI tool, not a human therapist, and it cannot respond to emergencies. If you have thoughts of self-harm, feel unsafe, or are in crisis, contact local emergency services or a crisis line instead of using the app.

faqs.q: What happens to my chat data in Wysa?
faqs.a: Wysa’s privacy policy explains that your chats are stored securely and used to provide and improve the service. Personal data is not sold to advertisers or data brokers. Aggregated and de-identified data may be used for analytics and research. If privacy is a major concern, you should read the full policy to understand how your data is handled.

faqs.q: Do I talk to a real person in Wysa?
faqs.a: The core Wysa experience is an AI chatbot. In some regions and programs, you can upgrade to human coaching or therapy, where trained professionals support you via text or other formats. The availability of human support depends on where you live and whether your employer or health plan has partnered with Wysa.

faqs.q: How long does it take to see benefits from Wysa?
faqs.a: Most digital CBT tools show benefit after a few weeks of regular use. With Wysa, you’re likely to notice the biggest impact if you check in several times a week, practice the exercises, and apply the skills in your daily life. Think of it like learning any new habit—it takes repetition over time.

Wysa is generally designed for ages 13 and up, but parents and caregivers should use their judgment and review the app first. For teens with significant mental health concerns, especially self-harm or suicidal thoughts, professional care is essential and should not be replaced by an app.

faqs.q: Does Wysa work without an internet connection?
faqs.a: No. Because Wysa relies on cloud-based AI and secure communication, you need an active internet connection (Wi-Fi or mobile data) to chat with the bot and use most tools.

faqs.q: Can I stop using Wysa anytime?
faqs.a: Yes. You can delete the app whenever you like and cancel any subscriptions through your app store or directly where applicable. If Wysa is provided by your employer or health plan, you may also be able to opt out of the program; check with your organization for details.
